newsitem.title: USA: Skater Baiul won't lose licence because of loophole.
newsitem.headline: Skater Baiul won't lose licence because of loophole.

text.p: A loophole in Connecticut's drunk driving laws has allowed Olympic figure skating champion Oksana Baiul to keep her driver's license, a state official said on Wednesday.

The loophole allows people who have been injured and taken to a hospital to escape what is usually an automatic license suspension, said Donald Bradley, an attorney in the Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) legal services division.
"If you want to use the word 'loophole in the law,' that's exactly what it is," Bradley told Reuters.

Baiul, 19, was taken to a hospital on Jan. 12 after a car crash in Bloomfield, Connecticut. The Ukrainian skater, who is two years younger than the state's legal drinking age, had a blood-alcohol content of 0.168 percent at the time of the accident; Connecticut's legal limit for adults is 0.10 percent.
Police have estimated she was driving at 97 mph (156 kph) where the speed limit was 45 mph (72 km), according to court documents.
Baiul on Monday asked to be enrolled in an alcohol education programme in an effort to avoid prosecution. A Connecticut judge will rule on her request on Feb. 4.
Several Connecticut legislators who have been active in seeking tougher drunk driving penalties have said they would seek to tighten up the law.
Baiul's lawyers could not immediately be reached for comment. They have said their client regrets the incident and that she would like to become a world spokesman in an anti-drunk driving campaign.
